newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson sees SAIF changes boosting profit.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson sees SAIF changes boosting profit.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co Wednesday said the changes in the recapitalization of the Savings Association Insurance Fund are expected to boost earnings going forward.

"The drop in deposit insurance premiums will add significantly to our company earnings going forward, and we have sufficient capital following payment of the special assessment to continue to satisfy the regulatory test for being a well-capitalized financial institution," Chairman Charles Rinehart said in a statement.
"Despite continued high credit costs, we are encouraged by declines in nonperforming assets and other signs of improvement in asset quality," he added.

As reported, Ahmanson posted a loss of $79.5 million or $0.85 a share in the third quarter versus a profit of $273 million or $2.03 per fully-diluted share a year ago. The latest period included charges of $8.3 million for the acquisition of 61 branches from the former First Interstate bank and $144.4 million for the recapitalization of the fund.
Without the charges, net income would have been $73.2 million or $0.56 per diluted share.
Net interest income totaled $306.2 million for the third quarter of 1996, compared with $314.4 million in the third quarter of 1995, mainly from a decrease in average interest earning assets.

The company said it added $19 million to its reserve for real estate investments in the third quarter of 1996, principally due to a revision in business plans for the disposition of one commercial project. REI assets now total $192.8 million, net of reserves.

During the third quarter of 1996, the company provided $35.8 million for loan losses, compared to $29.2 million in the third quarter of 1995. During the first nine months of 1996, the company provided $115.6 million for loan losses, compared with $81.2 million in the first nine months of 1995.

During the third quarter of 1996, nonperforming assets (NPAs) reached their lowest level since August 1995 and totaled $897.6 million, or 1.77 percent of total assets, compared with $916.5 million or 1.81 percent of total assets at Sept. 30, 1995.

Net loan charge-offs for the third quarter of 1996 totaled $34.7 million, compared with $33.8 million in the third quarter of 1995. For the first nine months of 1996, net charge-offs totaled $112.9 million, compared with $96.1 million in the first nine months of 1995.

In the third quarter of 1996, the company purchased 1.9 million shares of its outstanding common stock at an average price per share of $25.48. Of the $150 million authorized for the company's second round of purchase activity, $82.4 million remains. In addition, in the third quarter of 1996, the company redeemed its preferred stock, Series B. This redemption will contribute about $0.09 to annualized earnings per share.
